Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 45-year-old woman with one-day history of right-sided pleuritic back pain, dyspnoea, low-grade fever, and two episodes of haemoptysis; clinically stable on video exam. Impression: likely community-acquired pneumonia vs. pulmonary embolism; urgent same-day in-person chest assessment arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint & timeline  
  – Today: Sudden onset shortness of breath; sharp pain in right back when taking a deep breath.  
  – Two episodes of coughing up small amounts of blood today.  
  – Subjective “slight fever.”  
  – Palpitations/awareness of heartbeat.  
  – 2-week history of fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance.

• Review of systems (pertinent positives/negatives)  
  – Denies leg swelling, recent long-haul travel, known prior clots.  
  – No upper-respiratory symptoms apart from cough; no trauma reported.

• Past Medical History  
  – Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

• Medications  
  – Methotrexate (last dose this morning).

• Allergies  
  – No known drug or other allergies.

• Social / Preventive  
  – Non-smoker; desk-based office job.  
  – Lives alone in a flat; owns a cat.  
  – No recent travel.

Examination:
• Video-guided findings  
  – Radial pulse counted: ~66–74 bpm, regular.  
  – Capillary refill brisk.  
  – Oropharynx normal; no cervical lymphadenopathy.  
  – Appears well and hemodynamically stable.  
  – No direct chest auscultation, BP, RR, SpO₂ or temperature obtained.

Impression:
• Most likely: Community-acquired pneumonia – acute pleuritic pain, fever, cough with haemoptysis, immunosuppression from methotrexate.  
• Consider: Pulmonary embolism – pleuritic pain/haemoptysis, SLE hypercoagulability, though normal pulse and no provoking factors.  
• Alternative: Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis/DAH – on MTX, but presentation very acute and fever present.  
• Lung cancer considered unlikely given abrupt onset, non-smoker, and clinician discussion.

Plan:
• Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for:  
  – Full vital signs (BP, temp, RR, SpO₂) and repeat pulse.  
  – Chest and cardiovascular examination with auscultation.  
  – Assessment for need of oral antibiotics for presumed pneumonia.  
• Investigations anticipated (depending on exam):  
  – Possible chest X-ray and baseline bloods; consider D-dimer/CTPA if PE suspected.  
• No medications prescribed pending in-person assessment.  
• Provide patient with support line number to book appointment today.  
• Counseling: Explained low likelihood of lung cancer; advised red-flag return if worsening breathlessness, increased haemoptysis, high fever, chest pain, or collapse.  
• Follow-up: Review results and clinical course after face-to-face visit; consider repeat imaging if symptoms persist.

Quality checks
● Missing/expected elements: Objective vitals (BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature); lung & heart auscultation findings; full medication list (only MTX documented); immunization status.  
● Transcript/DDx conflicts: Patient name given as “Tracy Chapman” early, later addressed as “Doris” (likely transcription confusion). No other substantive conflicts.  
● Transcript quality: Adequate history; remote exam limited; some conversational overlap and name discrepancy; otherwise coherent.
